transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um, well, what finally made me come in today is that I just keep forgetting basic adult things. Like, paying my bills, returning emails for job interviews, actually showing up for appointments, or just... following through on regular errands. I recently finished school and I'm trying to get my life going, but this forgetfulness has started costing me real opportunities, so I knew I needed to talk to someone about it.
Do you find it hard to focus or stay on task even when you're trying your best, or does the forgetfulness usually happen when you're feeling stressed or down?

It's definitely an issue even when I'm trying my absolute best. It doesn't really seem tied to being stressed or down. 

Um, for example, I will sit down to update my resume or work on a coding practice problem, and I just get derailed so easily. A text notification, someone talking outside, or honestly even just a random thought about another task pulls me completely off track. I end up abandoning what I was doing, and it usually happens before I even notice what happened.
Do you often find yourself losing focus or getting distracted during everyday tasks, like reading, watching something, or even having a conversation with someone?

Um, I haven't really noticed that, to be honest. Like, if I'm watching a show or talking to a friend, I don't think I get distracted. I'm usually fine with that kind of stuff. 

It mostly just happens when I'm trying to do work or errands, like I was saying before. But for just regular conversations or watching things... no, I don't really think I have an issue with that.
When did you first start noticing these issues with forgetfulness and getting easily distracted? Were these problems that you experienced as a child, or did they start more recently?

Well, it's definitely not a new thing. Um, even back in elementary school, I had these issues. 

I remember my teachers would always write on my report cards that I was a bright student, but... they'd also say I was constantly losing my worksheets or rushing through the directions. And I guess I talked out of turn a lot, too. My desk was always just so messy that I literally couldn't find my assignments in it. So, yeah, it's been happening since I was a kid.

Do you find that you also have trouble staying organized or remembering things in other parts of your life, like at home, in social situations, or with personal projects—not just when you're working on job-related tasks or errands?

Um, honestly, I haven't really noticed it being a problem in those other areas. Like, in social situations or with my friends, I don't really forget things or lose track of what's going on. And if I'm working on a personal project—like something I'm just doing for fun—I'm usually fine staying on top of it. 

So, I don't think so. It really just seems to hit me the hardest when I have to sit down and do actual work or those errands I mentioned earlier.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms of forgetfulness, difficulty staying on task, and being easily distracted started in childhood and are most prominent during work or errands, which aligns with ADHD, Predominantly Inattentive Presentation. Other candidates (F41.9, F06.7, F33.9) are ruled out due to absence of significant anxiety, mood symptoms, or psychotic-like symptoms.
